title: Lisbon on Foot: Seven Hills, Seven Days

bestPeriod.avoid: July–August — 35°C on the calçada, Alfama unwalkable by noon, peak prices.

accommodation.note: Boutique guesthouse double, per-person share, Chiado or Príncipe Real

food.note: Tasca lunches €10–16, one €50–70 dinner, €6/day coffee and pastéis

transport.note: Navegante card, Sintra return, ferries, funiculars, airport metro

activities.note: Gulbenkian, MAAT, Azulejo, Jerónimos, two Sintra palaces

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — 8–12 km a day on steep basalt cobbles, 150–250 m cumulative ascent; hard on ankles, not on lungs.

gatewayAirport: LIS — Humberto Delgado; Metro Red Line to Alameda 20 min, taxi to Baixa 20–25 min (€15–20)
summary: Lisbon rewards people who accept that the city is a staircase. This week trades the tram-28 conveyor belt for a neighbourhood sequence: the Moorish tangle of Alfama and Mouraria, then the Pombaline grid and the literary hills of Chiado and Bairro Alto, then Príncipe Real, then the river — Belém's Manueline stonework west, Marvila's warehouse breweries east. Distances are short, gradients are not. A Sintra day breaks the week open with fog and Romantic follies. It suits travellers who want architecture and food weighted equally.

itinerary.title: Landing on the Grid: Baixa and Chiado
itinerary.morning: Metro to Baixa-Chiado, drop bags, walk the Pombaline grid from Praça do Comércio up Rua Augusta — note the standardised window bays, Manuel da Maia's prefab logic in stone. A *bica* standing at Confeitaria Nacional on Praça da Figueira, open since 1829.
itinerary.afternoon: The roofless **Convento do Carmo** (€7) is the truest surviving image of 1 November 1755. Then Museu Nacional de Arte Contemporânea–Chiado on Rua Serpa Pinto, and up via the **Elevador da Glória** to Miradouro de São Pedro de Alcântara.
itinerary.evening: **Taberna da Rua das Flores** (no. 103), no reservations — arrive 19:00, chalkboard menu, €25–35pp. Ginjinha at **A Ginjinha**, Largo de São Domingos, €1.60.
itinerary.dayStats: 5.5 km, 130 m ascent; Metro Red + Green; Navegante €0.50 + 24h pass €7.25; Carmo 10:00–19:00.

itinerary.title: Alfama and Mouraria end to end
itinerary.morning: Bus 737 from Praça da Figueira to **Castelo de São Jorge** (€15) for the 09:00 opening and empty ramparts, then walk down through Largo do Contador Mor.
itinerary.afternoon: Rua de São Pedro and Beco do Carneiro into lower Alfama; the **Sé** (Romanesque, 1147, twin fortress towers, cloister €5). Cross into **Mouraria** by Rua dos Cavaleiros for Largo da Severa and the grocers of Rua do Benformoso — the least gentrified inner quarter.
itinerary.evening: Fado at **Mesa de Frades**, Rua dos Remédios 139A, a tiled former chapel; 20:00 sitting, book 3–5 days ahead, ~€45 with food. Cheaper walk-in alternative: **Tasca do Chico**, Rua do Diário de Notícias 39.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.8 km, 210 m ascent; bus 737; castle €15, opens 09:00; fado 20:00–21:00 starts.

itinerary.title: Belém: Manueline stone, modern riverfront
itinerary.morning: Tram 15E from Praça da Figueira (25 min). **Mosteiro dos Jerónimos** on a 09:30 slot (€18 combined with Torre de Belém; church nave free). The two-storey cloister and Castilho's south portal are the reason to come.
itinerary.afternoon: **MAAT** (€11) — Levete's crouching pavilion plus the 1908 Central Tejo boiler hall, which is the better half. Torre de Belém from outside; the interior queue rarely repays 45 minutes.
itinerary.evening: **Cervejaria Ramiro**, Av. Almirante Reis 1 — garlic prawns, then a *prego* as dessert. No bookings; take a ticket, expect 30–50 min, €35–45pp.
itinerary.dayStats: 6.2 km flat; tram 15E ~€1.66; Jerónimos 09:30–18:00, closed Mon; MAAT closed Tue.

itinerary.title: Príncipe Real, Estrela, Gulbenkian
itinerary.morning: Up through **Praça das Flores** to **Praça do Príncipe Real** and its 1863 cedar canopy; Embaixada inside the neo-Moorish Ribeiro da Cunha palace. On to **Jardim da Estrela** and the 1790 **Basílica da Estrela** dome.
itinerary.afternoon: Metro Blue Line to São Sebastião for the **Calouste Gulbenkian** (€14, Founder's + Modern; free Sun after 14:00). Two hours minimum — the Lalique room, the Rembrandt wall, and Gonçalo Ribeiro Telles's garden.
itinerary.evening: **A Cevicheria**, Rua Dom Pedro V 129 (no reservations, leave your name, drink pisco next door), or **Cantinho do Avillez**, Rua dos Duques de Bragança 7, booked a week out, €40–55pp.
itinerary.dayStats: 7.1 km, 170 m ascent; Metro Blue; Gulbenkian €14, 10:00–18:00, closed Tue.

itinerary.title: Sintra day trip
itinerary.morning: Rossio 08:11 train, 40 min, ~€2.40. Bus 434 up to **Palácio da Pena** for a 09:30–10:00 slot (park + palace €20) — Ferdinand II's 1840s Romantic collage of Manueline quotation, Moorish tile and Bavarian battlement.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the **Castelo dos Mouros** ramparts (€12), then the **Palácio Nacional de Sintra** with its conical kitchen chimneys (€13). In heavy fog, swap for **Quinta da Regaleira** (€15) and its initiation well.
itinerary.evening: Back by 19:00. **Bistro 100 Maneiras**, Largo da Trindade 9 (book 2 weeks, €70–90pp) or petiscos at **Taberna Sal Grosso**, Calçada do Forte 22.
itinerary.dayStats: 9.4 km incl. Sintra hills, 320 m ascent; ~€4.80 train return; Pena last entry 18:00.

itinerary.title: Azulejos east: Xabregas, Marvila, Beato
itinerary.morning: Bus 794 to the **Museu Nacional do Azulejo** in the Madre de Deus convent (€8, closed Mon). The 23-metre panorama of pre-earthquake Lisbon upstairs explains what 1755 erased better than any text.
itinerary.afternoon: North into **Marvila/Beato**: Dois Corvos taproom on Rua Capitão Leitão, the Fábrica Braço de Prata warehouse, Underdogs Gallery's wall on Rua Fernando Palha. Industrial Lisbon converting itself in real time.
itinerary.evening: **Prado**, Travessa das Pedras Negras 2 — produce-led, book 2–3 weeks, €45–60pp. Late drink at Pensão Amor, Rua do Alecrim 19.
itinerary.dayStats: 8.6 km, flat; bus 794/210; Azulejo 10:00–13:00 & 14:00–18:00; taproom pints €4–5.

itinerary.title: Estuary morning and departure
itinerary.morning: Ferry Cais do Sodré → **Cacilhas** (10 min, ~€1.55) for the reverse skyline and lunch at **Ponto Final**, Rua do Ginjal 72, booked ahead. Or Elevador de Santa Justa at 08:30, before the queue.
itinerary.afternoon: Last pastéis at **Manteigaria**, Rua do Loreto 2 (€1.40, at the marble counter), then Metro Red Line to LIS from Alameda.
itinerary.evening: Flight out; a closing vermouth at Comida Independente, Rua Cais do Tojo 28, if the slot is late.
itinerary.dayStats: 4.5 km; ferry 10 min; airport 25 min from Baixa-Chiado with one change; allow 2 h before departure.

accommodationStrategy.name: Casa Balthazar
accommodationStrategy.description: Mid-slope between Baixa and Bairro Alto, so both are downhill and you never need a taxi. Private terraces, plunge pool, and a small lift up from Rossio that saves sixty steps a day. €160–210 double with breakfast; ask for a Tagus-facing room.

accommodationStrategy.name: Memmo Alfama
accommodationStrategy.description: The right base if Alfama is the priority: red-tiled pool terrace over the Tagus, in a lane no tour group reaches with wheeled bags. Steep approach — taxi to Largo de São Rafael on arrival. €190–260.

accommodationStrategy.name: Casa Amora
accommodationStrategy.description: Quieter and greener for a full week, with kitchenettes for the Mercado de Campo de Ourique haul and a flat ten minutes to Metro Rato. €130–180.

logistics.connectivity: Full EU roaming, no local SIM needed for EU residents. 4G/5G is complete; download offline maps only for the Pena woods, where signal drops.
logistics.emergency: 112 for everything. Tourist police post at Palácio Foz, Praça dos Restauradores. EU/EHIC applies; insurance still matters because timed monument tickets are strictly non-refundable.
logistics.weather: The *nortada*, a hard afternoon northerly, cools summer but leaves riverfront terraces cold after 19:00 even in June. Autumn downpours make calçada portuguesa genuinely slippery — rubber soles, never leather.
logistics.bookingWindows: Pena 5–7 days; Jerónimos/Belém 1–2 weeks; Prado and 100 Maneiras 2–3 weeks; fado houses 3–5 days. Gulbenkian, MAAT and Azulejo are same-day.
logistics.money: Euro, contactless everywhere, though small tascas prefer cash. Use Multibanco ATMs, not Euronet. Tip by rounding up, 5–10% at dinner. The *couvert* is chargeable — decline it.
logistics.transportRules: Validate on every boarding including trams and funiculars; inspectors work 28E and 15E hard. Some CP gates reject zapping for Sintra — buy at the Rossio counter if so. Santa Justa is €6.15 standalone but included in the 24h Carris pass.
logistics.permits: City tourist tax €4 per person per night, capped at seven nights, collected at check-out and usually absent from booking-site totals. Drones banned over the historic centre and all Parques de Sintra sites.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable and good. Real risks are pickpockets on tram 28 and at Santa Justa, and harmless drug-hawkers on Rua Augusta. Wet cobbles injure more visitors here than anything else.

proTips: Ride **tram 12E** on the same rails as the 28 for a shorter Alfama loop with a fraction of the crowd — or take the 28 eastbound from Martim Moniz at 07:15.
Load **zapping**, not the 24h pass, unless you'll make five-plus rides that day. Lisbon is a walking city; most days you use two.
For Pena, book the first slot, take bus 434 up and **walk down** through the Parque da Pena past the Chalet da Condessa d'Edla — the half everyone skips.
**Manteigaria over Pastéis de Belém** when time is tight: same custard tart, no 40-minute queue, and you watch the lamination through the window.
**Miradouro da Senhora do Monte** in Graça beats São Pedro de Alcântara at sunset and has a fraction of the buskers — 12 minutes uphill from Largo da Graça.
Most museums close **Monday** (Azulejo, Jerónimos, Ancient Art); the Gulbenkian closes **Tuesday**. Build Monday around the Castelo, Belém exteriors and Marvila.
If Sintra is fogged in before 11:00 — common in spring — reverse the day: Regaleira and the town palace first, Pena at 14:00 when cloud usually lifts.

raw.Walkable blocks: Alfama/Mouraria (Largo das Portas do Sol → Rua de São Pedro → Rua dos Cavaleiros, 1.8 km loop, 90 m ascent); Baixa/Chiado (Rua Augusta → Largo do Carmo, 1.2 km); Bairro Alto/Príncipe Real (Rua da Rosa → Praça das Flores → Praça do Príncipe Real, 1.6 km); Belém (Jerónimos → MAAT, 1.1 km flat); Marvila/Beato (Rua do Açúcar → Fábrica Braço de Prata, 1.4 km flat).
raw.Transit pass: the **Navegante Ocasional** card costs **€0.50** at any metro machine and holds one mode at a time — singles, a **24h Carris/Metro pass (€7.25)**, or **zapping** stored credit (~€1.66 a ride versus €1.80–€2.20 on board). You cannot hold zapping and a 24h pass together.
raw.Airport transfer: Metro Red Line (Aeroporto → Alameda, change Green for Baixa-Chiado), ~25 min, roughly €2.00–€2.50 with the airport surcharge. Bolt/Uber to Chiado €12–18.
raw.Booking timeline: Sintra's **Palácio da Pena** — 5–7 days ahead on parquesdesintra.pt, half-hour entry slots, 09:30–11:00 goes first. **Jerónimos + Torre de Belém** — 1–2 weeks on patrimoniocultural.gov.pt. Gulbenkian, MAAT and Museu Nacional do Azulejo take same-day walk-ups.
raw.Architectural focal points: Manueline at Jerónimos (Boytac and João de Castilho, 1501–1541 — rope, armillary spheres, artichokes in limestone); Pombaline seismic *gaiola* framing across the post-1755 Baixa grid; Mesnier du Ponsard's 1902 Elevador de Santa Justa; the 1969 Gulbenkian by Athayde and Cid; Amanda Levete's tiled MAAT wave-roof (2016).
raw.Eating structure: tascas at lunch (€10–16), one booked dinner mid-week (€45–70), pastelarias as fuel. Prado and Bistro 100 Maneiras want 2–3 weeks; Ramiro and Taberna da Rua das Flores take no bookings at all.
raw.Day trip: Sintra on the **CP Linha de Sintra** from Rossio, 40 min, ~€2.40 each way, departures every 10–20 min from 06:00.

sources.confidenceNotes: Museum admissions (Gulbenkian €14, MAAT €11, Azulejo €8, Jerónimos/Belém combined €18) and Sintra prices (Pena €20, Regaleira €15, Castelo dos Mouros €12) come from 2025–26 published rates and are revised each January — re-verify. The Sintra train fare is a zapping-rate approximation. Restaurant booking policies (Prado, Bistro 100 Maneiras, A Cevicheria, Ramiro) shift often. Mesa de Frades pricing is indicative. Tram 28 routing is periodically cut on the Graça section for works.
